title: "Maths for machine learning"
---

# Four areas cover almost everything

1. **[Linear algebra](maths-linear-algebra.qmd):** vectors, matrices, dot products, matrix multiplication. Data and neural network layers are all matrices, so this is the most important one.
2. **[Calculus](maths-calculus.qmd):** derivatives, partial derivatives, the chain rule. This is how models learn (gradient descent and backpropagation).
3. **[Probability and statistics](maths-probability.qmd):** distributions, expectation, variance, Bayes' rule. Needed for loss functions, uncertainty, and evaluating models.
4. **[Optimization](maths-optimization.qmd):** gradient descent and its variants. It's mostly calculus applied to "how do I make the error smaller?"

You do not need a full maths degree to start. You need a small working kit: enough linear algebra to read a layer, enough calculus to see how training moves, and enough probability to understand a loss.

<mark>Most of machine learning is this loop: make a prediction, measure the error, then move the parameters a little to make the error smaller.</mark> The symbols on the next pages are the shorthand for that loop.

Proofs can wait. First you want to know **what a formula is asking**.

# Reading order

1. **[ML math symbols, explained easy](maths-symbols.qmd)** — start here. One card for each common symbol ($\nabla$, $\mathbb{E}$, $\odot$, a norm, $\arg\max$, and a few extras), with a tiny numerical example and a NumPy line.
2. **[Linear algebra essentials](maths-linear-algebra.qmd)** — vectors, matrices, the dot product, and why a neural network layer is a matrix multiply.
3. **[Calculus essentials](maths-calculus.qmd)** — slope, partial derivatives, the gradient, the chain rule, and one step of gradient descent. Ties in with the [gradient primer](/ann/ann-activation-functions.qmd#a-gradient-primer) on the activation-functions page.
4. **[Probability and statistics essentials](maths-probability.qmd)** — expectation, variance, Bayes, likelihood, and why a cross-entropy loss is an average over the data. Ties in with [Naïve Bayes](/algorithms/algo-naive-bayes.qmd).
5. **[Optimization essentials](maths-optimization.qmd)** — the loss as a landscape, the update $\theta \leftarrow \theta - \eta\nabla L$, the learning rate, mini-batch, momentum, and Adam.

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
  A[Symbols] --> B[Linear algebra]
  A --> C[Calculus]
  A --> D[Probability and statistics]
  C --> E[Optimization]
```

Read them in any order if you only need one idea. If you are new, the list above is the shortest path.
